transcript:
Live from NPR News, I'm Dale Willman.
Chinese President Xi Jinping arrived home Saturday after three days of talks in Washington
with President Trump.
Munch of the meeting was focused on pomp and circumstance, but trade was also on the agenda,
including a two-month extension of a truce important to the U.S., as NPR's Emily Fang
tells us.
This trade truce is regarding rare earths, and this was a truce that was about to expire
this November, and it had stopped China from cutting the U.S. off completely from rare
earth elements, which China still dominates.
Now the U.S. and China have confirmed they've extended that by two months, so it expires
in January, but this is far shorter than both sides were hoping for, and per my reporting,
it was because mutual distrust has scuppered the possibility of a longer extension.
A nor'easter continues to affect New York City, with officials saying the worst is yet
to come.
Jessica Gould from member station WNYC has our story.
Senator Kathy Hochul has called for a state of emergency in New York City and surrounding
areas, urging people to stay home.
She says not to underestimate the storm following a calm stretch Saturday afternoon.
Don't take this, Lylee.
Don't tempt Mother Nature.
Don't risk your life.
The rain is expected to intensify overnight and through Sunday morning, with gusty winds
and coastal flooding.
And officials say a full moon could worsen flooding.
Already, a few residents and coastal queens work kayaking through the streets.
And videos show cars entirely underwater around a hotel in nearby Edgewater, New Jersey.
Officials are encouraging New Yorkers to avoid all travel through late Sunday morning.
For NPR News, I'm Jessica Gould in New York.
The storm has left tens of thousands of customers without power along the northeast coast and
caused flight cancellations throughout the region.
The Pope has wrapped up the Paris portion of his four-day trip to France with a massive
open-air mass in the center of that city.
In accordance with France's strict separation of church and state, President Macron did not
attend NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports.
One thousand choir singers from around France accompanied Pope Leo as he led the mass, which
was dedicated to the Virgin Mary and included communion for 40,000 people.
It was all broadcast on giant screens to the 800,000 people who had packed the Champs-Élysées.
The Pope called to deepen the quest for a meaningful life instead of ceding to the siren
call of consumerism.
70-year-old Parisian Sophie Paradis was there.
She says this Pope goes beyond religion in such troubled times.
It is very important for the universe.
He's a diplomatic Pope also.
Leo is in the pilgrimage site of Lourdes Sunday before heading to the eastern city of Mess
to speak in front of European leaders Monday.
Eleanor Beardsley, NPR News, Paris.
And you're listening to NPR News.
President Trump, Saturday, rejected an Iranian offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.
If the U.S. stopped its blockade of Iran, waved sanctions on Iranian oil sales and agreed
to a conditional cease-fire.
If those conditions were met, the Strait would reopen in seven days.
When rejecting the proposal, Trump told reporters that Iran is desperate to make a deal because
it's losing so badly.
The Cleveland Orchestra has gone on strike, as NPR's Eva Poucatch reports.
Concerts have been canceled, and the orchestra's European tour is also in doubts.
The Cleveland Orchestra is one of the big five American symphony orchestras.
Its musicians went on strike Friday.
The Cleveland Orchestra says the Musicians Union asked for a 25 percent increase in salaries
over the next three years, which the orchestra says it could not meet.
The Cleveland Orchestra was preparing for a nine-country European tour beginning in
Germany next week.
A decision on whether the tour will proceed will be made by Sunday evening.
Eva Poucatch, NPR News.
In college football, Oregon's quarterback Dante Moore left the field Saturday wearing
a neck brace after a rough hit by USC linebacker Desmond Stevens.
He was taken to a hospital for evaluation.
Stevens was ejected from the game.
Oregon went on to beat USC 41-27.
Number one Texas struggled before beating Tennessee by three points.
Number two Georgia and number three Notre Dame all won their games, but number four
Ole Miss lost to Florida 52-28.
Number 17 Iowa beat Michigan as time expired 20-19.
And Alcorn State beat Texas Southern in overtime 43-40.
I'm Dale Willman, NPR News.

topics.text: Chinese President Xi Jinping concludes three-day Washington talks with President Trump on trade
U.S. and China extend rare earth elements trade truce by two months until January
Nor'easter continues affecting New York City with worst weather expected overnight and Sunday morning
Pope concludes Paris visit with massive open-air mass attended by 800,000 people on Champs-Élysées
President Trump rejects Iranian offer to reopen Strait of Hormuz conditional on lifting blockade
Cleveland Orchestra musicians strike over salary dispute, canceling concerts and threatening European tour
Oregon quarterback Dante Moore injured in hit by USC linebacker Desmond Stevens, hospitalized for evaluation
Number one Texas beats Tennessee by three points in college football Saturday
